chapters.title: How the copy stays in sync
Fit with Azure, Microsoft 365 and Power BI

takeaways: A mirrored database is a live, read-only copy of an existing database inside Microsoft Fabric, kept current by tracking only changes instead of nightly pipeline jobs.
Mirroring storage and replication compute are free up to one terabyte per capacity unit, but querying is billed and a paused Fabric capacity stops replication.
Mirroring is not a backup, migration tool or two-way sync, and source-specific limits decide whether a given database can be mirrored at all.
hook: Your most valuable data is often locked in an operational database nobody can safely report on, and the nightly copy jobs that bridge the gap break at the worst moment. This episode explains Microsoft Fabric mirrored databases for data, BI and Microsoft 365 teams: how the near real-time copy works, what it costs and which limits trip people up.
